sections.h2: Cushing and the SPR are far below their historical peaks

chart.title: Cushing stands at 30% of its 2017 peak and the SPR at 42% of its 2010 peak
chart.sub: Current stock as a share of each series' historical peak, %.
chart.source: US EIA weekly petroleum status and annual workbooks.

sections.means: Cushing and the SPR are the two physical buffers behind the crude market, and both sit well below peak.
sections.todo: Refresh the Cushing figure, since the post's own update says stocks have risen to about 34% of peak.

sections.h2: US crude imports lean heavily on Canada, nearly ten times the next source

chart.title: Canada alone supplies US$90.16bn of crude, far ahead of every other partner
chart.sub: US crude imports by partner, 2025, US$ bn.
chart.source: US Census Bureau / USITC trade data, implied unit-value grade proxy.

sections.means: Pipeline-delivered heavy crude from Canada suits the Gulf Coast refineries that are built to run it.
sections.todo: Read the partner list as a grade story, not a supply-security story, when judging US crude dependence.

sections.h2: Gulf producers and the US are net petroleum sellers; India is the largest net buyer

chart.title: Only India, Mexico and Bahrain are net buyers, and India's deficit is the largest
chart.sub: US$ bn, net (exports minus imports), latest complete reported year per country. Basis differs by country.
chart.source: UN Comtrade public preview (HS, reporter-declared); DGCI&S TRADESTAT for India.

sections.means: The Gulf producers and the US export more petroleum than they import, while India is the largest net importer.
sections.todo: Read the Mexico position with care, because its gasoline import line does not reconcile with US export data.
